title: Lesson 8: How to Disciple Others
description: Someone once helped you follow Jesus. This lesson shows how to walk alongside another person the way Jesus walked with His disciples, so that what you have received keeps being passed on.

blocks.text: You have learned to pray, listen, serve, share, live for Jesus at work and school, and stand firm in a real spiritual battle. Growing Out is meant to bear fruit in other people, not only in you. This lesson is the next step: making space to sit down with someone as they follow Jesus, then sending them to help someone else.

blocks.title: Four Generations
blocks.text:
When Paul met Timothy in Lystra, Timothy was already a disciple with a good reputation among the believers (Acts 16:1-2). Paul invited him to travel and serve alongside him. Timothy heard Paul teach and watched how he lived through hardship. Years later Paul reminded him, "You, however, have followed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness" (2 Timothy 3:10).

Paul did more than give Timothy information. He shared his life and prepared Timothy to lead. Even when they were apart, Paul wrote to instruct and encourage him. Then Paul gave Timothy a charge that reached far beyond the two of them.
and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

Notice the four generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and others. Paul was helping Timothy depend on Jesus and preparing him for his own personal ministry. He sat with Timothy, then sent him to sit with others. In the same way, someone has helped you follow Jesus. This lesson is about how God might use you to disciple another person to become a disciple-maker.
8.1 - Who has helped you grow in love for God and others? What did that person do?
Jesus Calls Ordinary People to Make Disciples

Jesus chose twelve disciples "so that they might be with him and he might send them out to preach" (Mark 3:14). Before He ever sent them out, they studied Jesus' perfect balance of truth and love. They heard His teaching (word), watched His compassion for people (deed), and they practiced the way of Jesus. As they matured, He gave them appropriate challenges to serve, and when they came back, they were encouraged as they told Him all they had done and taught (Mark 6:30). Jesus was forming ordinary people who would carry His message and be sent to others.

After His resurrection, Jesus commanded His followers to make disciples, baptizing them and "teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you" (Matthew 28:19-20). The goal was never just that someone would know more Bible facts. Discipleship helps a person grow in love for God and love for others, and learn to obey Jesus in everyday life.

You may feel unqualified because you still have questions and still struggle with sin, but so did the people Jesus first called. You do not need to be a perfect Christian or have every answer. You just need to keep following Jesus, care about another person, and share what you are learning. And you will not do it alone. Jesus ends the Great Commission with a promise: "I am with you always" (Matthew 28:20).
Sit Down Together

Discipleship grows when people sit down together, whether it is one friend over coffee or a few others around a table in your small group. Sitting together gives people room to ask honest questions, face their struggles, practice obeying Jesus, and celebrate progress. Tap through the drawing below and watch what happens at one table.
Make SPACES

Did you see the word take shape? Make SPACES: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage, Send. These are five things you can actually do. The S at the end is not extra polish. After you encourage someone, you send them, and sending creates more spaces: spaces for discipleship, and spaces for growth in a relationship with Jesus. It is not a closed loop. It is a process that multiplies.
Study

Open God's Word and learn. Ask, "Would you like to do a Bible study with me?" Growing Together gives you a path to follow. Start with the lessons that fit the person's needs, whether that means the foundations in 101 or a topic from the 200 series. Read the lesson, look at Scripture, ask what it means, and pray. The goal is not to finish pages. It is to help someone know Jesus and love Him more.
Practice

Learning grows stronger when someone can try what they have learned. Model the skill first, then invite them to practice in a safe setting. After a lesson about sharing the gospel, you might say, "Let's practice sharing your testimony. You can share yours with me." Later comes Practice Leading: they lead a question or explain a Bible passage, and you help them prepare. They learn by watching, trying, and trying again.
Appropriate Challenge

Give a specific next step that fits the person's readiness. You might say, "I want to challenge you to start a conversation about Jesus with someone this week." A newer believer may be ready to pray aloud or share a testimony. Someone with more experience may be ready to lead part of a Growing Together lesson. A good challenge stretches someone without leaving them on their own. It is not yet Send. Send comes after you have walked with them and encouraged them.
Encourage

Follow up with care. Ask what happened, listen, pray, and celebrate the courage it took to try. You might say, "I'm so proud of you for taking that step. How did it go?" If the person struggled, encourage them without pretending it was easy. Help them learn and choose another step. Paul kept teaching and strengthening Timothy through his letters. Encouragement is not an extra after the real work. It is part of helping someone grow, and it prepares them to be sent.
Send

Then send them. You might say, "You are ready to sit down with someone else. Would you invite one person to begin Growing Together with you?" You are not handing them a title or asking them to become an expert. You are helping them care for another person the way someone cared for them. The person you send can use the same lessons and the same SPACES process. That is the movement of 2 Timothy 2:2: faithful people learning to teach others. One table becomes many. More spaces open for discipleship, and more spaces open for growth in Jesus.
8.2 - Think of one person at Neighborhood Church, at home, or in your 2nd Space. How could you sit down with them, walk SPACES, and one day send them?
From Learner to Disciple-Maker

The process grows with the person. At first you may lead most of a Growing Together lesson while the other person listens and asks questions. Soon, invite them to prepare and lead a small section. Practice with them before they lead. Give an appropriate challenge, then ask how it went and encourage them. Over time, let them take more responsibility. When they are ready, send them to sit down with someone else.

Who should you invite first? Paul told Timothy to entrust the message to faithful people. Look for someone who is faithful, available, and teachable. They do not need to know much or look impressive. They need a willingness to learn and make room for growth. Begin with one person, not a complicated program. Ask whether they would like to work through a study with you, perhaps once a week or every other week. Sit down. Walk SPACES. Then send.
8.3 - Who is one faithful, available, and teachable person you could invite to study Growing Together with you?
God Gives the Growth

Think of an orchard. A gardener can prepare the soil, plant, water, and care for a young tree. But the gardener cannot make it live. Paul wrote, "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth" (1 Corinthians 3:6). Your job is not to change another person's heart. Only God can do that. Your part is to love, sit down, open His Word, model obedience, give wise challenges, encourage, send, and depend on the Holy Spirit.

This is why discipleship takes patience. Some conversations will feel fruitful. Others will feel slow. Keep praying and keep caring. The aim is not to produce a person who can repeat your answers. It is to help someone love Jesus and others more deeply, serve in His church, and then be sent to help another person do the same.
8.4 - Which part of SPACES would you be most tempted to skip, and what would help you remember it?
Lesson 8 Review

Jesus calls ordinary people to make disciples, and He promises to be with you. Paul showed Timothy how faith can be passed from one generation to the next. You can make SPACES: Study, Practice, Appropriate Challenge, Encourage, Send. Sit down with one person, share your life, use Growing Together as a guide, and then send them so more spaces can open. God gives the growth.
In the next lesson, you will consider the people God places beside you in His mission, from your church to the ends of the earth.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
